manual_context.text: A rising vibration RMS accompanied by increasing kurtosis and a bearing housing temperature more than 10 C above the motor frame indicates advanced drive-end bearing wear. Schedule replacement within the next planned window; do not defer beyond 72 hours once kurtosis exceeds 5.

Where the expected cost of a planned intervention in the next low-load window is below the expected cost of run-to-failure, the planned window is the default recommendation and requires shift-engineer approval.

explanation_text: MTR-042 has an 81% calibrated probability of drive-end bearing failure within the 48-hour horizon. The strongest evidence is vibration RMS sitting 3.4 standard deviations above its high-load regime baseline, together with rising kurtosis (5.9) and a bearing-temperature slope of 0.42 C/h, which motor-maintenance.md section 4.2 Drive-end bearing wear identifies as the signature of advanced bearing wear. Under the configured plant-cost assumptions, maintaining in the next low-load window (2026-09-26 02:00-05:00 UTC) has an expected cost of $5,900 versus $8,400 to stop now and $46,700 to run to failure. The recommended action is to schedule bearing replacement for that window, consistent with plant-maintenance-policy.md section 3.1. The model warned a median 41.5 hours before failure on held-out machines, so the window falls inside its demonstrated lead time.
